title: Latent Context Prioritization Playbook
body:
Notes: rough playbook / brain-dump for a client-side "latent" context prioritizer. Goal = minimize tokens sent to hosted/dedicated inference while preserving downstream answer quality and latency SLOs.

Quick summary (tl;dr):
- Break client context into small segments (utterances, doc blocks, embeddings shards).
- Score each segment for "salience" using a cheap local model + heuristics.
- Apply TTL and staleness rules; maintain a compact recency-weighted priority queue.
- Package top-k segments (or a size-bounded prefix) with a lightweight provenance header for server-side merge.
- Provide a fallback: include a small global summary if uncertain.

Design constraints and tradeoffs (notes-to-self):
- Must run on client CPU / mobile; algorithms should be O(n log k) at worst.
- Avoid heavy float ops—prefer quantized dot-products or sparse lexical heuristics for low-power devices.
- Latency budget: non-blocking scoring that doesn't push user-visible latency >50ms on median device.
- Privacy boundary: do not rely on server-only signals for scoring. Keep scoring deterministic/local.
- Robustness: when model hallucination risk is high, prefer conservative inclusion of more context rather than aggressive pruning.

Segment model (v0): segmentation rules:
- primary: conversational utterance boundary (speaker change + punctuation heuristics)
- secondary: long-document block (<= 250 tokens per block)
- special segments: system prompts, pinned context, user-specified anchors (always include)

Salience scoring (sketch):
1) lexical-relevance score (lightweight): token overlap / fuzzy ngram hit with the current prompt keywords. Fast bloom filter / simhash quick wins.
2) recency boost: exp(-age / tau) where age = seconds since segment creation, tau (~1e5 s) tuned per workload.
3) engagement signal: explicit local signals (cursor position, selection), or whether the segment was recently edited.
4) semantic proxy: micro-embedding dot with prompt-proxy embedding using small on-device encoder (8-32d). If device missing, fall back to lexical.
5) structural bias: system messages or segments tagged as "pinned" get multiplier.
Aggregate: final_score = w_lex*lex + w_recency*recency + w_engage*eng + w_sem*sem + bias. Weights are tuned per product (defaults included below).

TTL and staleness policy (notes):
- Each segment carries created_at and last_active_at timestamps.
- If last_active_at older than staleness_threshold (e.g., 30d) drop unless pinned.
- Soft-evictions: demote score but still keep until memory pressure triggers actual removal.

Client data structures (simple):
- Segment entry: id, text_snippet (or compact token refs), compact_embedding (optional), created_at, last_active_at, tag_set, score_cache.
- Priority queue: top-k by score_cache (k dynamic by budget).
- LRU list for fast purge.
Implementation detail: store compact_embedding as int8 32-d vector using product quantization for mobile.

API shape (v0) — see lightweight envelope to server (text form example):
- request: { "prompt": "...", "context_segments": [ {"id":"s123","source":"client","text_preview":"...","approx_tokens":120,"score":0.82,"provenance_tags":["recent","selected"] }, ... ], "client_context_summary":"short: favorite topics: X; prior question: Y" }
Note: in actual SDK this will be binary-encoded for size. Server should treat context_segments as hints, not authoritative: it can fetch full content for dedicated/private deployments if configured.

Server-side acceptance rules (recommendation for runtime team):
- Respect segment.score but run a quick re-check with server-side canonical embeddings when available.
- If total appended tokens > model_max_ctx, apply server-side compaction (summary-then-include) or trim lowest-scoring segments.
- Emit telemetry: which segments were used, token delta, and quality signal via eval hooks (important for model-quality regression).

Example config DSL (client):
- prioritizer.v0.strategy = "latent-salience"
- prioritizer.v0.max_context_tokens = 1200
- prioritizer.v0.lex_weight = 1.0
- prioritizer.v0.sem_weight = 2.5
- prioritizer.v0.recency_tau_seconds = 86400
- prioritizer.v0.min_include_threshold = 0.15  # below this, not sent unless pinned
- prioritizer.v0.fallback_summary_tokens = 64

Heuristics for specific product flows:
- Conversational assistant: favor last N utterances (N tuned) + pinned system messages. Use semantic proxy more strongly.
- Documentation search: favor segments with named entities and high lexical overlap; reduce recency weight.
- Code assistant: favor code snippets with exact token matches + file path anchors; prefer smaller segment sizes (80 tokens).

Failure modes & mitigations (todo list):
- Too-aggressive pruning -> missing context -> hallucination. Mitigation: conservative lower bound on included tokens and add fallback_summary.
- Score drift across clients -> inconsistent behavior. Mitigation: periodic server-side re-scoring and telemetry-driven weight tuning.
- Privacy leak by over-summarization -> leak sensitive PHI. Mitigation: local PII-detection that redacts or avoids sending sensitive segments.

Telemetry (what to log):
- segment_count_sent, total_tokens_sent, median_segment_score, top_segment_ids, fallback_used (bool), response_quality_label (human or eval).
- periodic weight snapshots for A/B tuning.

Small experiment plan (MVP to validate):
1) A/B test on small cohort using lexical-only prioritizer vs naive last-N. Metrics: token reduction, latency, user satisfaction (CSAT), model-accuracy on canned eval prompts.
2) Add micro-embedding proxy on-device for half of cohort; measure delta in model accuracy vs token savings.
3) Iterate on config defaults and TTLs; roll to larger groups if stable.

Open questions / TODOs (action items):
- decide default embedding dims and quantization format for cross-platform compatibility. (Action: Arjun)
- representative prompt-keyword extractor design (cheap sketch vs on-device model). (Action: Sofia)
- privacy review checklist for client-to-server segment headers (security). (Action: Security team)
- server-side contract: what the runtime will guarantee when hint segments are provided. Need explicit API for "fetch full content if retained" in Dedicated/Private. (Action: runtime/product)

Appendix: quick ascii diagram of flow

[client app] -> segmentation -> per-segment scoring cache -> prioritize top-k -> envelope -> [SDK transmit] -> [server runtime] -> re-check & merge -> model input

Memos to self: keep this doc intentionally conversational; move polished spec to shared_drives/engineering/proposals once experiments validate.

Last rough defaults (for experiments):
- max_context_tokens: 1024
- lex_weight=1.0 sem_weight=2.0 recency_tau=86400 min_threshold=0.12
- default_segment_size=160 tokens

End of playbook draft.

---
Choppy notes:
- consider user opt-out flow: persistent toggle in privacy settings that disables client-side summarization and forces full context send (for enterprise).
- how to surface to SDK users: simple API call prioritize_context(prompt, budget_tokens) that returns list of ids + debug hints.
- store local scoreboard per-tenant to adapt to user's domain over time (but purge on uninstall).
